model: Vondrak, Capitaine & Wallace (2011) long-term precession, via ERFA (pyerfa)

poi.name: Ring Nebula
poi.desc: Glowing shell of gas thrown off by a dying Sun-like star.

poi.name: M56
poi.desc: Globular cluster of old stars about 32,000 light-years away.

poi.name: Great Hercules Cluster
poi.desc: The brightest globular cluster in the north: several hundred thousand stars.

poi.name: M92
poi.desc: One of the oldest globular clusters in the Milky Way.

poi.name: Hercules X-1
poi.desc: Neutron-star X-ray pulsar feeding on a companion star.

poi.name: Turtle Nebula
poi.desc: Small, bright planetary nebula.

poi.name: Beta Lyrae
poi.desc: Two stars so close they swap gas and eclipse each other every 12.9 days.

poi.name: Epsilon Lyrae
poi.desc: The 'Double Double': two pairs of stars bound together.

poi.name: Cat's Eye Nebula
poi.desc: Intricate planetary nebula almost exactly at the ecliptic's north pole.

poi.name: Draco Dwarf
poi.desc: Faint satellite galaxy of the Milky Way, rich in dark matter.

poi.name: Spindle Galaxy (M102)
poi.desc: Lens-shaped galaxy seen edge-on with a dust lane.

poi.name: Splinter Galaxy
poi.desc: Thin edge-on spiral surrounded by faint star streams.

poi.name: Tadpole Galaxy
poi.desc: Disrupted spiral with a 280,000-light-year tail of stars.

poi.name: Pinwheel Galaxy
poi.desc: Huge face-on spiral; host of supernova SN 2011fe and SN 2023ixf.

poi.name: Bode's Galaxy
poi.desc: Bright spiral galaxy about 12 million light-years away.

poi.name: Cigar Galaxy
poi.desc: Starburst galaxy; host of supernova SN 2014J.

poi.name: Ursa Minor Dwarf
poi.desc: Ancient, faint satellite galaxy of the Milky Way.

poi.name: NGC 188
poi.desc: One of the oldest open star clusters known, near the pole today.

poi.name: Polarissima Borealis
poi.desc: The galaxy closest to today's north celestial pole.

poi.name: IC 342
poi.desc: Large spiral galaxy hidden behind Milky Way dust.

poi.name: Cassiopeia A
poi.desc: Remnant of a supernova whose light reached Earth around 1680; the brightest radio source beyond the Sun.

poi.name: Tycho's supernova remnant
poi.desc: Debris of the 1572 supernova recorded by Tycho Brahe.

poi.name: 3C 58
poi.desc: Pulsar wind nebula, possibly the remnant of the supernova of 1181.

poi.name: CTA 1
poi.desc: Supernova remnant with a gamma-ray pulsar at its centre.

poi.name: Iris Nebula
poi.desc: Reflection nebula lit by a young hot star.

poi.name: Elephant's Trunk (IC 1396)
poi.desc: Large star-forming nebula with a dark pillar of gas.

poi.name: Bubble Nebula
poi.desc: Bubble blown by the wind of a massive young star.

poi.name: Fireworks Galaxy
poi.desc: Spiral with ten supernovae seen in a century, a record.

poi.name: Garnet Star (μ Cep)
poi.desc: Red supergiant, one of the largest stars visible to the eye.

poi.name: Delta Cephei
poi.desc: Prototype Cepheid: its pulsations measure cosmic distances.

poi.name: M52
poi.desc: Rich open star cluster.

poi.name: Cygnus X-1
poi.desc: The first widely accepted black hole: about 21 Suns of mass, in orbit with a blue supergiant.

poi.name: V404 Cygni
poi.desc: Black hole that flares in outbursts as it eats from a companion star.

poi.name: Veil Nebula / Cygnus Loop
poi.desc: Remains of a supernova that exploded roughly 10,000-20,000 years ago.

poi.name: North America Nebula
poi.desc: Glowing hydrogen cloud shaped like the continent.

poi.name: Cygnus A
poi.desc: Powerful radio galaxy with jets from a supermassive black hole.

poi.name: Crescent Nebula
poi.desc: Shell blown off by a Wolf-Rayet star.

poi.name: Blinking Planetary
poi.desc: Planetary nebula that seems to blink when you look away.

poi.name: Cygnus X-3
poi.desc: X-ray binary that can launch bursts of high-energy particles.

poi.name: Nova Cygni 1975
poi.desc: Bright nova of 1975, briefly a second-magnitude star.

poi.name: 61 Cygni
poi.desc: First star to have its distance measured (Bessel, 1838).

poi.name: M39
poi.desc: Loose open cluster in Cygnus.

poi.name: Eastern Veil
poi.desc: The brightest arc of the Cygnus Loop.

poi.name: Dumbbell Nebula
poi.desc: Bright planetary nebula in Vulpecula.

poi.name: NGC 6503
poi.desc: Dwarf spiral at the edge of the Local Void.

poi.name: NGC 6340
poi.desc: Lenticular galaxy in Draco.

poi.name: NGC 4236
poi.desc: Faint barred spiral in Draco.

poi.name: AM Canum Venaticorum
poi.desc: Two white dwarfs orbiting every 17 minutes.

poi.name: RR Lyrae
poi.desc: Prototype of the pulsating stars used to measure distances in the galaxy.

poi.name: Hercules galaxy cluster
poi.desc: Cluster of about 200 galaxies, 500 million light-years away.

poi.name: NGC 6229
poi.desc: Distant globular cluster in Hercules.

poi.name: Abell 39
poi.desc: Almost perfectly spherical planetary nebula.

poi.name: NGC 2403
poi.desc: Spiral galaxy with many star-forming regions.

poi.name: Heart Nebula
poi.desc: Large emission nebula in Cassiopeia.

poi.name: Pacman Nebula
poi.desc: Star-forming nebula in Cassiopeia.

poi.name: Bow-Tie Nebula (NGC 40)
poi.desc: Planetary nebula around a hot Wolf-Rayet-type star.

poi.name: NGC 6939
poi.desc: Old open cluster in Cepheus.

poi.name: Hubble Deep Field
poi.desc: Tiny patch where Hubble found about 3,000 galaxies in 1995.

poi.name: Whirlpool Galaxy
poi.desc: Spiral galaxy pulling on a smaller companion; host of three recent supernovae.

poi.name: M106
poi.desc: Spiral with an active supermassive black hole and a water maser disc.

poi.name: Owl Nebula
poi.desc: Round planetary nebula with two dark 'eyes'.

poi.name: Surfboard Galaxy (M108)
poi.desc: Edge-on barred spiral near the Owl Nebula.

poi.name: M109
poi.desc: Barred spiral galaxy in Ursa Major.

poi.name: Markarian 501
poi.desc: Blazar: a black-hole jet pointed almost straight at us, bright in gamma rays.

poi.name: 3C 345
poi.desc: Quasar with a jet that appears to move faster than light (an illusion of geometry).

poi.name: NGC 6207
poi.desc: Spiral galaxy next to the Great Hercules Cluster in the sky.

poi.name: Abell 2256
poi.desc: Merging galaxy cluster with giant radio relics.

poi.name: NGC 6217
poi.desc: Barred spiral near the north ecliptic pole.

poi.name: Draco Trio (NGC 5985)
poi.desc: Brightest of a trio of galaxies in Draco.

poi.name: Sunflower Galaxy
poi.desc: Flocculent spiral with patchy arms.

poi.name: AG Draconis
poi.desc: Symbiotic star: a white dwarf feeding on a red giant.

poi.name: NGC 6742
poi.desc: Small planetary nebula in Draco.

poi.name: NGC 6633
poi.desc: Open cluster in Ophiuchus.
